title: Regional node catalog & telemetry patterns
content:
Purpose:
This note collects patterns for a regional, telemetry-driven node catalog (what I’m calling the `catalog ledger`) used by the control plane and routing layer. Focus: how we represent node capability, how we grade health from signals, and how we replicate/serve that information across regions for low-latency routing decisions.

High level goals:
- Single source-of-truth for node capabilities and soft capacity at the regional level (not per-request discovery).
- Fast lookups for routing (latency/cost tiers, GPU capability matching) with bounded staleness.
- Telemetry-derived health grades that drive automated fallbacks and model-variant routing.
- Minimal cross-region chatter: use CRDT-like summaries + per-region authoritative heartbeats.

Constraints we must respect:
- Control plane must not add 50ms to request path. Lookups should be cacheable at edge/proxy or in the request router.
- Node metadata size must be small (labels + a small capability fingerprint), no heavy per-node blobs.
- Telemetry can be noisy (transient OOMs, short interrupts). Need smoothing and clear soft/hard thresholds.

Data model (proposal):
- Node key: region:pool:node-id (e.g. us-west1:gpu-rtx-a:node-01234)
- Core labels (flat kv strings):
  - hw.gpu.vendor=nvidia|amd
  - hw.gpu.model=A100|H100|RTX8000
  - hw.gpu.memory_gb=80
  - hw.cuda.compute=8.0
  - infra.instance_type=p4d.24xlarge
  - runtime.qos=dedicated|shared|preemptible
  - capabilities=triton,kvcache,quant-int8 (comma-separated short list)
- Capability fingerprint: short hash of (model-abi, kernel-hotpatch-version, quant-profile-id) — used to quickly detect compatible node sets for a model.
- Soft_capacity: integer representing estimated concurrent gen slots (derived from telemetry + static per-GPU cap).

Heartbeat / telemetry payload (what nodes publish to regional control plane):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- cpu.util_pct (rolling 1m)
- gpu.util_pct (per-device summarized)
- gpu.mem_free_gb
- available_slots_estimate (derived by node local agent)
- running_model_ids (short list up to N)
- recent_fail_count (O=last 5m model-run failures)
- last_reboot_ts
- health_flags (bitmask-like: 0 = ok, 1 = noisy-oom, 2 = high-temp, 4 = cuda-driver-mismatch)

Health grading (regional control plane algorithm - high level):
- Compute a 0..100 health_score per node using exponential smoothing over a 3-window (1m, 5m, 15m) of composite signals.
- Components: slot-failure-rate (40%), gpu-temp/thermal-throttle events (20%), mem-pressure (20%), heartbeat-staleness (20%).
- Map to categories: HEALTHY (score >= 80), DEGRADED (50-79), UNAVAILABLE (<50).
- Soft quarantine: DEGRADED nodes still appear in the catalog but with reduced soft_capacity and a "penalty" multiplier applied to routing cost. UNAVAILABLE nodes are excluded from active routing and considered for maintenance actions.

Routing policy integration (how router uses the catalog ledger):
- Router does a two-step decision for each request: 1) regional prefilter using capability fingerprint + labels (fast), 2) cost/latency ranking using health_score + dynamic latency probe (if enabled).
- Preference order: local region healthy nodes -> local region degraded nodes -> remote region healthy nodes (if latency/SLO permit) -> fall back model-variant routes (smaller model or cached response).
- Cost calculus: routing_score = base_latency_est + health_penalty_ms + cost_penalty_usd. health_penalty_ms derived from (100 - health_score) * factor.

Multi-region replication model:
- Per-region authoritative catalogs: each region maintains its own ledger and heartbeats.
- Global summarizer: periodically (every 30s) aggregate per-region summaries (capacity buckets, fingerprint counts, top-k latency percentiles) and replicate these to other regions. Summaries are small and drive cross-region fallback decisions without exposing per-node data.
- On failover/evacuation: destination region(s) can request full node lists from source region on-demand (auth + rate-limited).

Service discovery API (control plane endpoints):
- GET /regions/{r}/catalog/query?capabilities=triton&gpu=A100&min_slots=2 -> returns candidate nodes or pools with capacity estimates (cached result TTL = 5s).
- GET /regions/{r}/catalog/summary -> capacity buckets + fingerprint counts (for cross-region planner).
- POST /regions/{r}/nodes/{node}/heartbeat -> node telemetry (ingested by region agent).
- GET /regions/{r}/nodes/{node}/health -> latest graded health + last_seen timestamp.

Health signal smoothing and anomalies:
- Use EWMA windows and also an anomaly detector (lightweight): if running_model_ids changes dramatically or failure spikes > 5x baseline, emit an "anomaly" tag and increase quarantine aggressiveness for 2m.
- Backfill: when heartbeats drop out, mark node as STALE after 30s, UNAVAILABLE after 90s. These thresholds tuned for our typical pub/sub propagation time (kafka+local agent).

Labeling conventions & governance:
- Keep labels low-cardinality. Avoid free-form owner/team labels on catalog level; map owner -> infra-team via a separate registry to prevent label explosion.
- Label audit job weekly: find labels with >100 unique values and flag for normalization.

Operational playbooks (examples):
- Node flapping (short OOMs then recover): automatically mark DEGRADED and reduce soft_capacity by 70%. Alert to oncall only if failures persist beyond 15 minutes.
- Thermal spike: if gpu-temp > 95C reported 3x within 5m, mark UNAVAILABLE and schedule a maintenance ticket with collected diagnostics.
- Cross-region capacity shortage: global planner picks remote region candidates using summary counts and pre-warms routing caches in edge proxies.

Integration points and telemetry stack:
- Ingest heartbeats via a regional kafka topic -> consumer writes to regional catalog DB (compact key-value store). Use Prometheus/OpenTelemetry for time-series; catalog stores only last-known summary points to keep lookups fast.
- Use vectorized TTL caches in routers to reduce control-plane hits; cache invalidation driven by heartbeat changes to fingerprint or health category.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we version capability fingerprints across rolling kernel/driver updates? Do we allow backward compatibility mapping tables?
- Can we offload some matching to edge proxies to avoid router trips for small requests? Cost vs consistency tradeoff.
- Need a short-pulse epidemiological test run (10% traffic) to validate health scoring windows.
- Define schema for running_model_ids (privacy + size limits).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an attempt to be pragmatic: small per-node metadata, region-authoritative heartbeats, smoothed health scores, and global summaries for cross-region planning. The model is intentionally conservative on staleness to avoid oscillation in routing.
- Feedback requested particularly on the health scoring weights, summary replication interval, and API TTL values.
